item.title: After his Reflecting Pool vandalism case is dismissed, David Hearn looks for closure
item.description: The ex-Olympian accused of damaging the reflecting pool tells NPR the experience has been "Orwellian" and "Kafkaesque." And it's not over yet: His lawyers are fighting to close the case permanently.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump and RFK Jr. try again to upend vaccines for kids
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on Monday about vaccines, saying children should get fewer. His administration has been blocked in the courts from changing the vaccine schedule.

item.title: 'The Nerd Reich' tracks the 'unmasking of Silicon Valley's true politics'
item.description: Journalist Gil Durán argues that a small circle of Silicon Valley billionaires and venture capitalists have concluded that democracy is in their way — and that they should be governing in its place.

item.title: Does spending money make you feel bad? Read this comic
item.description: If spending — or not spending — money makes you feel shame or regret, you might be grappling with financial guilt. Financial planner Lauryn Williams breaks down three types and how to deal.

item.title: Decades of abuse revealed at Michigan art school. And, the Iran war's impact on midterms
item.description: A new report has revealed decades of alleged abuse at an elite art school. NPR spoke with one of the victims. And, Iran is playing the long game with negotiations, which could impact midterms.

item.title: People with disabilities say Medicaid income limits can stifle career advancement
item.description: Medicaid will have new work requirements next year. But some people with disabilities, who already work, say they'd like to work more, but risk losing their Medicaid coverage if they earn too much.

item.title: In a competitive Maine Senate race, women voters could be the deciders
item.description: The race between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson is one of this year's most high-profile Senate contests. To win, both candidates will need support from an especially powerful voting bloc: Maine women.
